title: A fast and sensitive isocratic high performance liquid chromatography method for determination of guaraná (Paullinia cupana) flavan-3-ols
author: Yonekura, Tamura

steps.title: Prepare calibration standards
steps.instruction: Prepare ten standard solutions for each of the five analytes (catechin, epicatechin, procyanidin B1, procyanidin B2, caffeine) covering the linearity range 0.195–100 nmol mL⁻¹. Use the same solvent as for sample extracts and inject 20 µL of each standard onto the isocratic HPLC‑UV system (210 nm).

steps.title: Assess linearity
steps.instruction: Run the ten calibration standards on the isocratic HPLC‑UV (210 nm) and plot peak area versus concentration for each compound. Verify that the correlation coefficient (r²) is ≥0.999 for all five compounds and fit a zero‑intercept regression (y = a·x).

steps.title: Calculate LOD and LOQ
steps.instruction:
Acquire 48 chromatograms of blank basal media (HBSS) and measure baseline noise. Compute the limit of detection (LOD) as 3 × noise and the limit of quantification (LOQ) as 10 × noise for each analyte. Report values for injection volumes of 40 µL (basal media) and 20 µL (in‑vitro digesta):
- Basal media (40 µL): LOD = 0.019 nmol mL⁻¹ (catechin), 0.030 nmol mL⁻¹ (epicatechin), 0.028 nmol mL⁻¹ (ProB1), 0.030 nmol mL⁻¹ (ProB2), 0.043 nmol mL⁻¹ (caffeine); LOQ = 0.062, 0.100, 0.092, 0.100, 0.144 nmol mL⁻¹ respectively.
- In‑vitro digesta (20 µL): LOD = 0.044, 0.063, 0.067, 0.073, 0.105 nmol mL⁻¹; LOQ = 0.148, 0.211, 0.223, 0.243, 0.350 nmol mL⁻¹ respectively.

steps.title: Spike matrices for recovery
steps.instruction: Prepare triplicate spiked samples of blank in‑vitro digesta (soluble fraction) and blank basal medium (HBSS). Spike catechin, epicatechin and caffeine at 1.56, 12.5 and 50 nmol mL⁻¹; spike procyanidin B1 and B2 at 0.78, 6.25 and 25 nmol mL⁻¹. Keep the spiked solutions on ice until analysis.

steps.title: Analyze spiked samples
steps.instruction: Inject the spiked samples (same injection volume as used for standards, 20 µL) onto the isocratic HPLC‑UV system under the same chromatographic conditions as the calibration run. Record peak areas for each analyte at 210 nm.

steps.title: Calculate recovery and precision
steps.instruction: For each analyte and concentration level, calculate recovery (%) as (measured concentration / spiked concentration) × 100. Compute intraday %RSD from the three replicates prepared on the same day and interday %RSD from the nine replicates (three replicates on two separate days). Expected recovery ranges are 97.2–109.4 % and both intraday and interday %RSD values are <4 % for all compounds.
